papers.title: An empirical derivation of the average dust attenuation law at 2<z<7
papers.abstract: Dust attenuation affects galaxy SEDs and introduces uncertainties in star formation rates, stellar masses, and metallicities. Direct spectroscopic constraints at early cosmic epochs were limited before JWST. We derive the average dust attenuation law of massive (log10(Mstar/Msun) > 9) star-forming galaxies at 2 < z < 7 using JWST spectroscopy. We combine JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy from JADES with deep multi-wavelength photometry from the ASTRODEEP-JWST catalogues. For approximately 120 mass-selected galaxies with reliable Balmer decrement (Halpha/Hbeta) measurements, we stack SEDs in bins of Balmer optical depth and derive the selective attenuation curve following Calzetti et al. (1994). JWST/MIRI photometry extends the wavelength coverage into the near-infrared (NIR). The resulting curve spans 0.16-1.14 microns in the rest frame and is well described by a smooth function. We derive R_V approximately 3.98, with Delta R_V = 0.16 indicating its sensitivity to the adopted long-wavelength extrapolation. The average attenuation law agrees remarkably well with the local starburst relation in slope and normalisation, but appears systematically flatter in the ultraviolet than several intermediate-redshift determinations. We find no significant evidence for a 2175 Angstrom UV bump. Our results provide a direct empirical constraint on the average dust attenuation law of massive star-forming galaxies at 2 < z < 7. This analysis exploits the combined spectroscopic and photometric reach of JWST. Despite variations among individual galaxies, the ensemble-average behaviour agrees with the local starburst relation, suggesting that the main mechanisms governing dust attenuation were already operating at early cosmic times. The relatively shallow UV slope may reflect differences in dust-star geometry, radiative-transfer effects, or effective grain-size distributions among galaxy populations.
papers.comments: 16 pages. Accepted for publication in Astronomy and Astrophysics

papers.title: Probing mass inflation in polymerized vacuum regular black holes via colliding null shells
papers.abstract: We derive a class of inner-extremal regular black hole solutions characterized by a degenerate inner horizon. These geometries arise as polymerized vacuum configurations inspired by loop quantum gravity and constitute effective quantum-gravity solutions that admit a Birkhoff-type theorem, rendering them unique within the considered framework. We show that such inner-extremal horizon configurations exist only for a finely tuned value of the mass determined by the parameters of the theory. Building on this construction, together with the corresponding non-degenerate regular black hole solutions, we perform a generic analysis of the mass inflation phenomenon in four-dimensional spacetimes using a colliding null-shell setup near the inner horizon. We identify the conditions under which mass inflation becomes significant and examine how the presence of a minimal length scale affects this behavior, with particular emphasis on the case where such a scale is motivated by loop quantum gravity. Finally, we comment on the stability of these configurations under the null-shell perturbations considered in our analysis.

papers.title: Dyonic black holes supporting nearly-black self-gravitating thin shells
papers.abstract: It has recently been revealed that dyonic black-hole spacetimes of a quasitopological non-linear electrodynamic field theory may be characterized by discrete radial regions with the property $dg_{tt}(r)/dr=0$ in which spherically symmetric massive {\it test} shells (Dyson shells with negligible self-gravity) can be supported in static equilibrium states. In the present paper we prove that the dyonic spacetimes of the non-linear electrodynamic field theory may also be characterized by the presence of radial regions with the dimensionless property $d[r\cdot g_{tt}(r)]/dr\to0^+$ in which massive {\it self-gravitating} thin shells that are on the verge of becoming black holes can be supported in static equilibrium states. Intriguingly, it is proved that the discrete radii of these self-gravitating nearly-black Dyson shells are universal in the sense that they are independent of the masses of the central supporting dyonic compact objects.
papers.journal_ref: Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics 10, 048 (2026)

papers.title: Silicate cosmic dust grain collisions in the interstellar medium: A molecular dynamics study
papers.abstract: (abridged) We aim to predict the most important parameters for grain-grain collision outcomes in models of interstellar grain population evolution: the threshold velocities for shattering and vaporization, and the resulting distributions of grain sizes. We use molecular dynamics simulations which evolve the dynamics of each atom in a dust grain to explore the outcomes of collisions between silicate grains of radii $a \in [5,50]~Å$ at velocities 0.1-20 km/s. We run simulations of grains with two materials: amorphous SiO$_2$ and an amorphous silicate of composition suggested by Draine \& Hensley (2021). With these simulations, we quantify the collision velocity dependence of shattered and vaporized mass fractions, and the resulting size distributions of shattering products. We find grain shattering thresholds are $\sim$6 km/s for both materials, a factor of $\sim$2 higher than the canonical value for silicates of 2.7 km/s from Tielens et al. (1994) and Jones et al. (1996). The size distributions of shattered products are generally not consistent with the power law distributions predicted by Jones et al. (1996), but the physical reasons for these discrepancies remain uncertain. The Tielens et al. (1994) expressions fail to predict the fraction of shattered or vaporized material observed in our numerical simulations, over-predicting the shattered fraction and under-predicting the vaporized fraction, except for the most massive grains we simulate, where the predicted vaporized fraction agrees reasonably well. The model of Hirashita \& Kobayashi (2013) similarly fails to match the simulations. We provide updated shattering velocity thresholds for nanoscale silicate grains, which suggest that the smallest astrophysical dust grains composed of silicate materials may be more robust to shattering in the interstellar medium than previously assumed.
papers.comments: Under review at A&A. This version withdraws our claim of an error in the threshold expression of Tielens et al. (1994); the expression is correct. The alternative threshold values we derived from that claim have been removed and the discussion updated accordingly. Simulated thresholds are unchanged

papers.title: Probing freeze-in dark matter using Bose-Einstein condensate in neutron star
papers.abstract: Neutron star (NS) is one of the most promising astrophysical targets to probe non-gravitational interaction of dark matter (DM) with visible matter. Their compactness makes them an ideal object which can capture particle DM efficiently over its lifetime using the DM-nucleon scattering cross-section. If DM particles are bosonic, then the captured DM population may form a Bose-Einstein condensate at the center of the NS, increasing the DM density significantly. In this work, we study the phenomenology of such scenario with enhanced DM annihilation rate due to the increased density in a condensate. The enhanced DM annihilation makes the NS surface `hotter' than in the standard cooling scenario. We show that the annihilation rate is enhanced by a factor of $\mathcal{O}(10^{15}-10^{20})$ if DM forms a condensate without large self-interaction, and DM with freeze-in value annihilation cross-section can heat up the NS to higher temperatures, bringing it within the reach of James Webb Space Telescope. It also allows us to probe DM-nucleon scattering cross section within the neutrino fog regime which will complement the terrestrial direct detection searches. Moreover, the enhanced annihilation from the condensate changes the lower limits on s-wave DM annihilation cross-section for capture-annihilation equilibrium and the formation of a black hole inside the NS. Finally, we show an example of a scalar DM model where such small annihilation and DM-nucleon scattering cross sections can generically arise.
papers.comments: 25 pages, 8 figures, one new figure and a section added, matches published version in JCAP

papers.title: Energy extraction from NED-deformed rotating black holes via the Comisso-Asenjo reconnection process
papers.abstract: We study rotating black holes in general relativity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics (NED), focusing on an axisymmetric solution with deformation parameter $g$. On the spherical seed, weak-field lensing via the Gauss-Bonnet method and the shadow radius yield a spin-insensitive bound by enforcing a conservative $\sim 10\%$ tolerance on the Sgr A* ring size, namely $g/M \lesssim 1.26$. In the eikonal regime we derive analytic quasinormal-mode shifts, even in $g$, and obtain an independent ceiling consistent with the shadow constraint. For the rotating geometry, we provide closed-form ZAMO scalars, chart horizons and the ergoregion, and analyze equatorial geodesics (photon orbits and ISCO). We then formulate the Comisso-Asenjo reconnection channel in the ZAMO frame, identify the negative-energy window, and integrate the extracted power over the allowed radii; from the tolerated fractional departure from the Kerr power we define a spin-dependent extraction bound $g_\delta(a\mid\sigma_0,\xi)$. Taken together, the QNM/shadow ceiling and the extraction bound appreciably narrow the admissible region for $g/M$ in the $(a/M,g/M)$ plane, so even within our deliberately simplified, single-layer equatorial setup, the two complementary probes already provide informative constraints on NED deformations, testable with present data and upcoming horizon-scale and ringdown campaigns.

papers.title: The Continuum Limit Analysis of Causal Fermion Systems for Curved Spacetimes
papers.abstract: We construct the causal fermion system for globally hyperbolic spacetimes starting in the framework of algebraic quantum field theory. The fermionic projector is identified with the one-particle density operator of a quasi-free Hadamard state. The ultraviolet regularization is built into the fermionic projector via a chart-independent $i\varepsilon$-regularization scheme. The continuum limit analysis is developed in globally hyperbolic spacetimes. It is shown that the Euler-Lagrange equations of the causal action principle are satisfied in this setup if and only if the coupled Einstein-Dirac equations hold.

papers.title: The Life and Death of Stars That Capture Primordial Black Holes
papers.abstract: Primordial black holes (PBHs) in the asteroid mass window ($10^{17}-10^{23}\,{\rm g}$) remain viable dark matter candidates and can be captured by stars. We develop the first global framework for the evolution of stars that capture PBHs, combining analytic calculations, stellar evolution models, 3D general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations, and Monte Carlo population synthesis. We find that the fate of these systems bifurcates: PBHs that form an accretion disk before consuming the host drive explosive disruption, whereas PBHs captured too late or growing too slowly consume the star quietly. Capture is dominated by three-body interactions with planetary or stellar companions. For a solar-type host with a Jupiter analog, inspiral within a main-sequence lifetime requires $M_{\rm BH}^{\rm crit}\gtrsim 10^{22}\,{\rm g}$, while lighter PBHs generally require tighter companions. Once deposited at the center, the PBH grows through inefficient quasi-spherical Bondi accretion; if it reaches the angular-momentum threshold before consuming the host, the inflow circularizes into a disk. Our Monte Carlo calculations yield sizable quiet-consumption and explosive-disruption populations, with final PBH masses $M_{\rm BH}\sim0.01-1\,M_\odot$ and disk-forming PBH spins $a_\ast\approx0.8$. Disk formation is the point of no return: disk winds and relativistic jets of $\sim10^{45}-10^{50}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$ disrupt the star within minutes. The resulting transients may include a $\sim$day-long UV/blue signal, radio afterglow, and, if the jet escapes, an X-ray-flash/low-luminosity gamma-ray-burst (XRF/llGRB) signal. For an $O(1)$ PBH dark matter fraction and optimistic capture assumptions, the event rate can reach that of llGRBs. The low-mass, high-spin remnants offer a complementary PBH probe and possible source for subsolar BH mergers.

papers.title: Detecting Tidal Resonances in Binary Neutron Stars
papers.abstract: As a binary neutron star inspirals due to the emission of gravitational waves, the rising tidal frequency resonantly excites vibrational modes. These oscillations are seismological probes of the rich stellar interior, yet it remains to be established whether gravitational-wave interferometers can measure them. Here, we present the first fully Bayesian study of the capability of the Einstein Telescope to detect tidal resonances. We simulate one year of observations and analyse the 200 loudest signals. We find that the Einstein Telescope can identify resonant modes and is sensitive to gravitational-wave phase shifts as small as $\Delta \Phi \approx 0.03$ for favourable events. We further show that neglecting resonances can bias the inferred tidal deformabilities. These results establish tidal resonances as a measurable route for asteroseismology with future detectors.
papers.comments: 6 pages, 3 figures. Accepted for publication in Phys. Rev. Lett

papers.title: A dark-matter-sensitive orientation clock near rotating black holes
papers.abstract: A coherent triaxial structure has an intrinsic orientation clock because rotation about its intermediate principal axis is unstable. I ask how this clock changes when the structure moves on a circular equatorial orbit near a rotating black hole in an effective dark matter (DM) environment. The calculation uses a comoving orthonormal tetrad, the electric part of the Riemann tensor, Euler--quaternion dynamics, and the conversion from proper time to stationary coordinate time. The clock shift separates exactly into a local proper-time response and a geometric time-conversion response. I compute a direct grid of 600 DM models for Einasto, regularized cored Navarro--Frenk--White, and Hernquist profiles. Across the scanned domain, the total fractional frequency shift lies between about $-3\times10^{-7}$ and $-3\times10^{-4}$. For the fiducial body model, most of the shift comes from the time conversion. Synthetic timing tests show that a shift near $10^{-4}$ is recoverable only when the clock is highly coherent and its Kerr baseline is known independently. This gives a theoretical timing diagnostic and a synthetic observational forecast. I do not fit real data.
papers.comments: 24 pages, 13 figures, 2 tables. Substantially expanded and fully rewritten version, adding direct numerical validation, robustness tests, nonlinear dynamics, and synthetic timing forecasts. To appear in IJGMMP

papers.title: Complete Relational Description of Spin in a Quantum Background
papers.abstract: The standard description of the state of a spin in quantum mechanics presupposes externally fixed directions -- a classical background. Can a spin be fully described instead in relation to other quantum mechanical systems? Poulin suggested twenty years ago group averaging over rotations the joint state of a fundamental spin and a reference spin with large angular momentum which, however, yields a classical bit in a probabilistic mixture. We revisit this idea and show that when the quantum reference system is augmented to \emph{two} large spins, the standard quantum mechanical description of a spin is recovered in the limit of large quantum numbers for the reference system.
papers.comments: 7 + 8 pages. v2: added a few references, v3: mistakes corrected in a comment (IV.B) and an appendix (B.3), added a recent reference, and some minor and typo corrections

papers.title: Polarization-Dependent Photon Propagation, Quasinormal Modes, and Gravitational Lensing in Higher-Curvature Effective Theories
papers.abstract: We investigate the impact of higher-curvature corrections on photon propagation within an effective field theory framework and their observational consequences in strong gravitational fields. We consider polarization-dependent modifications to photon trajectories in static and spherically symmetric spacetimes, focusing on Schwarzschild and Reissner--Nordström black hole backgrounds. Using the geometrical optics approximation, we derive the effective metrics governing photon propagation and study the resulting polarization-dependent shifts of the photon sphere. We compute the corresponding quasinormal modes in the eikonal limit and analyze their polarization dependence. We further investigate gravitational lensing, focusing on polarization-dependent corrections to the deflection angle in both weak- and strong-field regimes. In the strong-deflection regime, we find that even perturbatively small EFT corrections modify the coefficient of the logarithmically divergent part of the deflection angle, resulting in a potentially observable difference from the uncorrected case. This suggests that strong gravitational lensing may provide a sensitive probe of small higher-curvature corrections. While extracting EFT information directly from QNM frequencies is more subtle, QNMs may provide complementary information to gravitational lensing in future studies. Our results establish a framework for probing higher-curvature effects through polarization-dependent strong-field observables.
papers.comments: 43 pages, 8 figures. arXiv admin note: substantial text overlap with arXiv:2605.27953

papers.title: A New Scaling of Neutron Star Tidal Deformability for Directly Probing the Central Equation of State Parameter
papers.abstract: The dimensionless tidal deformability, $\Lambda$, of neutron stars (NSs), inferred from gravitational-wave (GW) observations, has thus far been used primarily to constrain the pressure of dense matter near twice nuclear saturation density, leaving the core equation of state (EOS) largely inaccessible to inspiral-phase GW observations. We show that a fundamental central EOS parameter can be probed directly through $\Lambda$ using a perturbative analysis of the dimensionless stellar-structure and tidal-response equations formulated in terms of scaled intrinsic variables, without invoking any specific EOS model. We uncover a remarkable EOS-insensitive scaling relation between $\Lambda$ and the central EOS parameter $\rm{X}\equiv P_{\rm c}/\varepsilon_{\rm c}$, where $P_{\rm c}$ and $\varepsilon_{\rm c}$ denote the central pressure and energy density, respectively. The relation is validated against a broad ensemble of physically viable EOSs. Applying it to tidal deformabilities inferred from events such as GW170817 enables a direct determination of $\rm{X}$. By adopting the previously established effective upper bound $\rm{X}\lesssim0.381$, we infer a tight lower bound, $\Lambda_{\rm{TOV}}\gtrsim9.1^{+0.5}_{-0.5}$, for maximum-mass NSs along stable mass-radius sequences, quantitatively demonstrating that even the most compact stable NSs remain distinctly separated from black holes, for which $\Lambda_{\rm{BH}}=0$. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized connection between inspiral-phase tidal deformability and the central EOS parameter $\rm{X}$, establishing a direct link between GW observables and the microphysics of ultradense matter in the strong-gravity regime. The resulting scaling establishes inspiral-phase tidal deformability as a direct and largely model-insensitive probe of the central EOS parameter $\rm{X}$, and hence of key properties of NS cores.
papers.comments: Title slightly revised. Accepted for publication in Phys. Rev. D (2026)

papers.title: Gravitational-wave responses and noise correlations in geometric time-delay interferometry
papers.abstract: Space-based gravitational-wave observations will probe the formation and growth of massive black holes and the evolution of compact binaries in the millihertz band. We develop a geometric-link representation of time-delay interferometry using six round-trip and six non-round-trip two-link blocks. Starting from the one-way Doppler response, we derive the elementary block responses and a dictionary that expresses 45 known second-generation combinations in terms of these blocks and residual one-way measurements. Representative Michelson and Relay observables admit compact forms, from which analytical sky-averaged tensor responses are obtained for a fixed, equal-arm constellation. We also derive the noise covariance of the blocks, retaining cross-spectra between blocks that share measurement streams. The resulting noise spectra agree with direct one-way assembly. We apply this formulation to a narrowband compact-binary signal in an equal-arm LISA instrument model. For the Relay example, neglecting the shared-link cross-spectrum changes the low-frequency noise scaling and overestimates the conditional Fisher uncertainties in amplitude or distance by factors of 10.71 at 1~mHz and 3.37 at 3~mHz.

papers.title: Unveiling the Milky Way with a Gaia DR3 census of OB-type stars within 2 kpc. I. Tracing local Galactic structure, massive star-forming regions and core-collapse supernova progenitors
papers.abstract: O- and B-type stars are young and hot, thereby serving as vital tracers of the star formation and spiral arm structure of the Milky Way. At the dusk of the \textit{Gaia} DR3 era, a high-confidence and accurate catalogue appears timely. We have characterized 105,971 OB-type stars (T$_{\rm eff} >$ 10,000 K) within 2 kpc from the Sun, using an astro-photometric Bayesian inference tool. Our map unveils a complex view of the young stellar populations across the thin disk, with prominent large-scale features such as the Cepheus Spur, the Giant Oval Cavity, and a segment the Sagittarius-Carina arm all visible. Their inhomogeneous spatial distribution implies that massive star formation has taken place clustered across a few highly concentrated regions. We find a correlation between the overdensities of OB-type stars and young open clusters, and attribute departure from it to extinction effects. We identify 4200 stars as model-dependent core-collapse supernova (ccSN) or direct-collapse black hole (BH) progenitor candidates, including 6 ccSN progenitor candidates within 125 pc -- the maximum radius within which a ccSN explosion could be harmful to Earth's biosphere -- but our analysis suggests none of them exploding within the next 5 Myrs. Finally, we anticipate more evolved OB-type stars to collapse to form BHs within the next 1 Myr than ccSN progenitors will explode, despite the former's much scarcer number. A possible interpretation is a recent star formation burst in the local Milky Way, consistent with overdensities of ccSN progenitor candidates in Cyg OB2 and the Sagittarius-Carina arm.

papers.title: Entropic Chaplygin-Gas cosmology and late-universe tension diagnostics
papers.abstract: We investigate an entropic generalized Chaplygin-gas (gCg) cosmology in which a single dark fluid accounts for both dark matter and dark energy. We constrain the model using DESI baryon acoustic oscillations, redshift-space-distortion measurements, compressed Planck 2018 distance and lensing information, and Type Ia supernova likelihoods with PantheonPlus+SH0ES (PPS) and DES--Dovekie. For Planck+DESI+RSD+PPS, the entropic gCg model yields a Hubble constant of $H_{0}=68.64\pm0.52\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and the amplitude of matter fluctuations parameter of $S_{8}=0.797\pm0.021$, compared with $H_{0}=67.31\pm0.28\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and $S_{8}=0.809\pm0.021$ in $\Lambda$CDM. The simultaneous upward shift in $H_{0}$ and downward shift in $S_{8}$ occurs in the directions required for a partial alleviation of both tensions. We also show that when PPS is replaced by DES--Dovekie, the parameter shifts are smaller, the best-fit improvement is negligible, and the Bayesian evidence favours $\Lambda$CDM. Thus, the entropic gCg model provides a potentially interesting simultaneous shift of the Hubble constant and the matter-clustering amplitude, but its statistical support depends on the adopted supernova likelihood.
papers.comments: 21 pages, revised version, 10 figures, 5 tables. Accepted version for publication in the European Physical Journal C (EPJC)

papers.title: Observational Evidence for Anisotropic Metal Excess around Galaxies
papers.abstract: The exchange of matter and energy between galaxies and their surroundings drives the cosmic baryon cycle, yet mapping metal transport remains an observational challenge. While simulations predict that galactic winds escape anisotropically along minor axes, evidence for chemical enrichment in neighboring galaxies is limited. We analyze 1,433 galaxy pairs from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument survey and detect a gas-phase metallicity excess of 14.6% $\pm$ 3.7% to 24.2% $\pm$ 2.6% in neighbors aligned with the minor axis of massive primary at projected separations of 15--60 kpc, qualitatively consistent with IllustrisTNG simulation. Permutation tests indicate that this excess varies from a marginal detection ($>$92% confidence) at closer separations (15--30 kpc) to a significant signal ($>$98% confidence) at intermediate separations (30--60 kpc). Here, we show that these results provide empirical constraints on galactic feedback models and are consistent with a scenario where anisotropic outflows can enrich nearby galaxies, a mechanism that complements other environmental processes.
papers.comments: 26 pages, 3 figures. Published in Nature Communications

papers.title: VAPOLA - A multiyear, multiband polarization survey of AGNs and Sgr A* at millimeter wavelengths with ALMA II. Spectropolarimetric properties and their evolution from 2017 to 2023
papers.abstract: We present a systematic analysis of the spectropolarimetric properties of a sample of 39 active galactic nuclei and Sagittarius A* observed with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array during five VLBI campaigns between 2017 and 2023. We characterize the compact cores in total intensity and polarization, focusing on the behavior or the linear polarization fraction (LP), electric vector position angle (EVPA), and Faraday rotation measure (RM) over time and spectral domains. We investigate both individual objects--such as M87, Sgr A*, 3C273, and 3C279--and ensemble properties of different source classes, including flat-spectrum radio quasars, BLLac objects, and other active galaxies. While total intensity and spectral index are generally stable on weekly timescales, polarization properties often exhibit strong variability, with significant day-to-day changes in LP, EVPA, and RM. Several sources display large EVPA rotations accompanied by variations in LP and RM, in some cases coinciding with flaring activity. We observe that the magnitude of RM increases with observing frequency for all sources for which we have reliable multi-band measurements, consistent with Faraday rotation arising in a magnetized sheath surrounding the relativistic jet, although an origin in the accretion flow--particularly in the case of Sgr A*--cannot be ruled out.
papers.comments: Accepted for publication in A&A; 38 pages, 18 figures, 20 tables

papers.title: Reissner-Nordstrom in the Bertotti-Robinson-Bonnor-Melvin electromagnetic field
papers.abstract: The magnetic Reissner-Nordstrom black hole embedded into the Bertotti-Robinson magnetic field is presented. Then it is used, as a seed, to generate, through the Harrison transformation of the Ersnt's equations, the Reissner-Nordstrom metric in the Bertotti-Robinson-Bonnor-Melvin magnetic field. Special cases generalising, the vacuum hairy type I Schwarzschild solution is discussed. The local equivalence between various forms of the Schwarzschild-Bertotti-Robinson is shown by exhibiting the explicit diffeomorphism.
papers.comments: 18 pages, v2: some typos corrected, magnetic potential simplified

papers.title: Penrose process in radiating Kerr-Vaidya black holes: efficiency, energy transport, and the viability boundary
papers.abstract: We study single-particle Penrose extraction from a rotating black hole whose mass decreases in time, described by the ingoing Kerr-Vaidya metric, imposing exact four-momentum conservation at the decay. We prove that the local efficiency is bounded by the instantaneous Kerr value, through a covariant bound that reduces to the Bardeen-Press-Teukolsky limit at the horizon, and we derive an exact transport law, dE/dtau = -dm/dt (r/Sigma) p_r^2 for fixed spin parameter, by which every timelike geodesic gains energy while the hole loses mass. The net energy gain therefore splits into a local Penrose term and two transport terms, which we compute numerically as functions of spin and mass-loss rate for two mass-loss laws. With fixed spin parameter, extraction is possible only below a critical rate alpha_crit(a) = (M-a)/Delta v, set by the approach of the hole to extremality; with fixed a/m no such boundary exists. The transport law extends to the Kerr-Newman-Vaidya family, and the regime where the dynamics matter is shown to lie far outside astrophysical mass-loss rates.

papers.title: Galaxy Protoclusters as Drivers of Cosmic Reionization: II. Te-Based Metallicities of Lyman-α Emitters
papers.abstract: Context. Protoclusters at reionization are thought to host a significant fraction of the cosmic star formation rate density, making them crucial for the timing and topology of reionization. The gas-phase metallicity, a key tracer of galaxy evolutionary stage, can now be measured directly in the early Universe with JWST. Aims. We measure the gas-phase metallicity of Lyman-$\alpha$ emitters (LAEs) in the LAGER-z7OD1 protocluster at $z\approx6.93$ via the direct ($T_e$-based) method using the [O III]$\lambda$4363 auroral line, and combine it with stellar masses to constrain the mass-metallicity relation (MZR) in dense environments. Methods. We use JWST/NIRSpec MSA G395H spectroscopy, derive metallicities with self-consistent analytic prescriptions, and propagate the dust-extinction uncertainty into an asymmetric error budget via Monte Carlo simulations based on the observed Balmer decrements. Stellar masses come from BEAGLE SED fitting of JWST/NIRCam and UltraVISTA photometry. Results. We obtain five secure [O III]$\lambda$4363 detections and one upper limit, with 12+log(O/H) $\approx$ 7.2-8.0. The weighted spectral stack yields 12+log(O/H) = $7.76^{+0.06}_{-0.05}$, ~0.26 dex higher than stacks of LAEs at similar redshifts from JWST surveys. However, the MZR fit gives a slope $\gamma$ = 0.232 +/- 0.214 and normalization $Z_0$ = 7.888 +/- 0.199, placing our sources below the established MZR of normal galaxies and recent protocluster baselines at $z\sim5-7$. Conclusions. The higher metallicity relative to general LAEs suggests accelerated assembly driven by the overdensity, while the offset below the MZR points to a complex interplay between mass build-up and gas accretion. Since we target actively star-forming LAEs, we are likely capturing a phase of pristine gas inflow from the intergalactic medium that fuels star formation but dilutes the interstellar media of these protocluster members.

papers.title: Collisional excitation of SiC$_6$ by helium: cross sections, rate coefficients, and astrophysical implications
papers.abstract: Rotational transitions of SiC$_6$ with $j=26$--$40$ have been detected in IRC+10216, but collisional rate coefficients for SiC$_6$ with He or H$_2$ were previously unavailable. We present rate coefficients for SiC$_6$ rotational excitation by He, calculated using a two-dimensional potential energy surface (PES) at the RCCSD(T)-F12 level under the rigid-rotor approximation. Close-coupling (CC) calculations were performed for low rotational levels, while the coupled-states (CS) method was used for higher levels. Convergence tests were conducted, and CC and CS scattering cross sections were compared. The CS rate coefficients cover rotational levels up to $j=40$ and temperatures of 3--60\,K. Although CC and CS rate coefficients differ by up to a factor of $\sim 2$ for some transitions, particularly those affected by weak coupling and resonances, they yield nearly identical excitation and brightness temperatures for the high-$j$ transitions examined, including $19\rightarrow18$. These results support the reliability of the CS method for non-LTE modelling of the high-$j$ transitions considered, for which CC calculations are computationally impractical. We use reduced-mass scaling of the SiC$_6$--He rate coefficients to estimate those for SiC$_6$--H$_2$ and model the observed transitions. A $\chi^2$ analysis of the observed line fluxes, excluding heavily blended features, yields a best-fitting of $n(\mathrm{H_2})=4.33\times10^5$\,cm$^{-3}$ and $N(\mathrm{SiC_6})=8.11\times10^{11}$\,cm$^{-2}$. The latter agrees excellently with the previous observational estimate of $(7.9\pm1.5)\times10^{11}$\,cm$^{-2}$, supporting the consistency of our non-LTE modelling with observational constraints.

papers.title: Logarithmic corrections to massive particle trajectories for the classical soft log theorems at leading order in $G$
papers.abstract: We study the logarithmic corrections to the asymptotic trajectories of massive particles. These corrections enter the calculation of the soft-log sector of the radiative field at null infinity in four-dimensional gravitational scattering. We first isolate the part of the metric which enters the particle equations of motion. We show that the nonlinear source can only affect this sector through homogeneous modes on the hyperboloid, and that matching to the proposed soft tower implies that these modes vanish, except for the first mode. We show that this mode cannot affect the trajectory coefficients at leading order in $G$. We then invert the matter energy-momentum tensor on the particle worldlines to obtain the trajectory coefficients at leading order in $G$ and at every logarithmic order using Legendre polynomials. The first two coefficients reproduce the known results at orders $G$ and $G^2$.

papers.title: Structure and evolution of cosmic voids within DESI DR1
papers.abstract: Ongoing stage IV galaxy surveys such as DESI or Euclid offer an unprecedented amount of information to study the large-scale structure of the Universe by mapping tens of millions of galaxies. Within the context of cosmic voids, already released and future catalogues will help better understand the void structure and evolution as well as the cosmological model constraints derived from their statistics. With the recent DESI Data Release 1, our aim is to obtain a new void catalogue that allows us to study the properties of cosmic voids at different redshifts, hence providing insight not only on their structure but also on their evolution. We select the DESI BGS and LRG samples for this study. Before the void-finding process, the data goes through a preprocessing pipeline tackling redshift space distortions and reconstructing the mildly non-linear velocity field. After that, the new AVISM void finder is applied to the preprocessed data, obtaining two void catalogues in different redshift bins (0.1 < z < 0.3 and 0.4 < z < 0.8), both within a 1400^3 cMpc^3 cube. We successfully recover N_BGS = 1114 and N_LRG = 216 clean voids with sizes up to ~ 65 cMpc. The void size function, 3D shape variables, density profiles, and linear bias are obtained and analysed. Both the size function and the density profiles obtained are in agreement with previous theoretical studies. The expected mass depletion in void evolution is shown by the evolution of density profiles. We obtain a roughly constant linear bias inside r < Re with mean values of 1.31 +/- 0.02 and 2.14 +/- 0.04 for BGS and LRG, respectively. Both void catalogues are publicly released.
papers.comments: 17 pages, 14 figures; accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics

papers.title: Consistently Reproducing Early Galaxy Observations and 21-cm Signal during the Epoch of Reionization
papers.abstract: In the standard cosmological model, galaxies forming within dark matter haloes are the primary drivers of the Epoch of Reionization (EoR). The complex physics of galaxy formation introduces scatter in the relation between halo mass and star-formation activity, with implications for the production and escape of ionising photons. In this work, we implement a stochastic source model in our cosmological radiative transfer simulations. We calibrate our model against the high-redshift ultraviolet luminosity function observed by JWST and observational constraints on Lyman-continuum leakage to constrain the ionising escape fraction. We find that stochastic star formation redistributes ionising emissivity toward lower-mass haloes, producing a more fragmented ionisation topology and delaying the growth of the largest ionised regions relative to the deterministic, observationally calibrated model. However, when the two models match total ionising photon production, their global neutral fractions and 21-cm power spectrum remain nearly indistinguishable, despite small differences in the morphology of individual ionised regions. Additionally, we establish a unified framework that lets us apply source models derived from computationally expensive hydrodynamical simulations (SPICE, FIRE-2 and Thesan) and investigate their impact on large-volume reionisation simulations, extending their prescriptions to scales of >100 Mpc. We find that these prescriptions produce distinct ionisation topologies and 21-cm statistical signatures, even when their global reionisation histories are similar. Our results highlight the importance of combining physically motivated galaxy formation prescriptions from hydrodynamical simulations with large-volume radiative transfer simulations to interpret forthcoming 21-cm observations and constrain the sources of cosmic reionisation.

papers.title: Beyond the Disc--Spheroid Dichotomy at $0.6 < z < 8.0$: Evidence for a Morphological Indeterminacy Regime from JWST
papers.abstract: Galaxy morphology is a fundamental tracer of galaxy assembly, but its characterization becomes increasingly uncertain in the early Universe. We investigate morphological classifications across different methodologies over the redshift range $0.6 < z < 8.0$, using JWST observations of 15,567 galaxies with 6,099 synthetic galaxies from IllustrisTNG. To quantify morphology without relying on visual labels or prescribed light profiles, we use an unsupervised-supervised hybrid machine-learning approach based on the non-parametric MEGG system, which combines the second moment of the light distribution, Entropy, Gini, and Gradient Pattern Analysis. We find that parametric and non-parametric classifications remain broadly consistent at $z < 2.5$, but diverge systematically at higher redshift. We identify this epoch as the Morphological Indeterminacy Regime (MIR), in which classical disc and spheroidal categories no longer provide a unique description of the galaxy population. The fraction of mixed-interpretation galaxies increases with redshift, reaching $F_{\rm MIR} \sim 0.55$ at $z > 2.5$. Cross-domain and projection-invariance tests show that the classifications are stable and insensitive to data set and viewing angle. In the interval $2.5 < z < 8.0$, MIR galaxies occupy an intermediate stellar-mass regime (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 9.7$), between low-mass discs (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 9.5$) and massive spheroids (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 10.1$), while irregular systems have stellar-mass distributions similar to those of MIR galaxies. We interpret these results as evidence that morphological indeterminacy is a characteristic feature of galaxy assembly in the early Universe, reflecting a population of dynamically young systems that have not yet settled into the classical Hubble sequence.

papers.title: The DARWIN Project: Cosmological Simulations of Galaxy Formation down to Dwarf Scales in Diverse Environments
papers.abstract: We present the DARWIN project, a suite of cosmological simulations with RAMSES to study dwarf-galaxy formation and evolution across diverse environments. DARWIN-1 is a full-box simulation in a cubic volume of $(65.5\,{\rm cMpc})^3$ with a minimum cell size of 500pc, while DARWIN-2 comprises zoom-in simulations of 24 field regions and a Milky Way analog connected to a filament, reaching 62.5pc resolution. The simulations employ baryonic physics tailored to their aims. For DARWIN-2, we include radiative transfer in three photon energy bands to trace hydrogen and helium ionization. DARWIN-1 reproduces the cosmic star formation rate density and galaxy stellar mass functions reasonably well at $z>1$. Both simulations broadly reproduce observed stellar mass-halo mass relations, chemical abundances, star-formation surface densities, and black hole-galaxy scaling relations. At lower redshift, DARWIN-1 shows an excess in the number density of massive galaxies, although the inferred stellar content of massive halos depends on the definition of galaxy stellar mass. Other systematic differences arise from spatial resolution, feedback efficiency, and environmental selection. To facilitate comparison with observations, we generate mock images using the radiative transfer codes SKIRT and Powderday. We also explore a machine-learning approach to mitigate resolution-driven biases in the dwarf galaxy properties of DARWIN-1 using the higher-resolution DARWIN-2 simulations. The DARWIN simulation suite therefore provides a comprehensive numerical framework for studying the formation, evolution, and internal physics of dwarf galaxies in a cosmological context.
papers.comments: 33 pages, 18 figures, submitted to ApJ, any comments welcome

papers.title: The Central Molecular Zone of our Galaxy, a chemical complexity factory: first interstellar detections of molecules towards G+0.693
papers.abstract: The Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) of our Galaxy is a prime laboratory for interstellar chemistry because of its extreme conditions, such as shocks and high cosmic-ray ionisation rates. It is an efficient factory of molecules, with many species first discovered in CMZ sources. This document reviews key results from the study of the CMZ G+0.693-0.027 molecular cloud. Using ultra-sensitive broadband spectral surveys together with laboratory spectroscopy, more than 140 molecules have been identified, including 28 detected for the first time in the interstellar medium (ISM). These discoveries include prebiotic precursors of biomolecules, increasingly complex members of known molecular families, molecules containing periodic third-row elements (S, P, Na, Mg), high-energy stereo- and structural isomers, and new cations. Overall, these findings extend the known limits of interstellar chemical complexity and highlight the CMZ's potential to provide the molecular ingredients for prebiotic chemistry.
papers.comments: Part of "Traversing the Galactic Center in Space and Time Proceedings IAU Symposium No. 405", M. Zajaček, T. Jerábková, V. Karas, R. Schödel & P. Suková, eds
